text.p: Lehman Bros analyst Mitchell Speiser said he lowered his recommendation on McDonald's Corp to outperform from buy.
-- The analyst also said he trimmed his 1997 earnings estimate to $2.45 from $2.52 and the 1998 view to $2.80 from $2.90. He also lowered the 12-month share price target to $55 from $60.
-- McDonald's shares were off 1/4 to 48-3/8 in morning New York Stock Exchange trade.

-- Reasons of the actions, derived from the analyst's research note, include the company's "U.S. business is in disarray; (the) $0.55 rotational sandwich promotion, at lunch and dinner, (is) to be scrapped after only six weeks."

-- "Still like long-term fundamentals and McDonald's dominating presence outside of the United States, but overall weakness in operations and increased uncertainty as to the strategic direction of the U.S. business will limit meaningful upside," according to the note.
-- "Expect management overhaul in U.S. business, in marketing and operations, (and) benefits to the bottom line will take time," the analyst's note states.
